Chapter 3 Data overview

This chapter describes the selected Microflora Danica panel before diversity analyses. All summaries are computed from the committed files loaded in the data preparation chapter.

3.1 Panel at a glance

overview_numbers <- data.frame(
  Measure = c("Samples", "Habitat classes", "Representative MAGs / 95% ANI clusters",
              "Phylogenetic tree tips", "Sample dates", "Distinct 10 km grid cells",
              "Detected representatives per sample, median (range)",
              "Zero entries in abundance matrix"),
  Value = c(
    nrow(overview_samples), length(habitat_levels), nrow(genome_metadata),
    ape::Ntip(genome_tree),
    paste(format(range(overview_samples$date), "%Y-%m-%d"), collapse = " to "),
    length(unique(overview_samples$cell.10km)),
    sprintf("%.0f (%d–%d)", median(detected_per_sample),
            min(detected_per_sample), max(detected_per_sample)),
    sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * mean(overview_abundance == 0))
  )
)
knitr::kable(overview_numbers)
Measure Value
Samples 360
Habitat classes 8
Representative MAGs / 95% ANI clusters 5518
Phylogenetic tree tips 5518
Sample dates 2014-10-16 to 2023-01-27
Distinct 10 km grid cells 251
Detected representatives per sample, median (range) 114 (4–298)
Zero entries in abundance matrix 97.7%

The abundance matrix contains relative abundances within the published MFD MAG profile, not sequencing counts or the fraction of all DNA. A detected representative means a strictly positive value in that profile. This threshold includes very small reported values, so detected richness should be interpreted with that sensitivity in mind.

3.2 Geographic coverage

The selection contains 45 samples per habitat class. The table shows the observed coordinate span and the number of occupied 10 km grid cells within each class; grid-cell counts need not sum to the panel total because classes can share cells.

habitat_rows <- lapply(habitat_levels, function(h) {
  d <- overview_samples[overview_samples$habitat_label == h, ]
  data.frame(
    Habitat = h,
    Samples = nrow(d),
    `10 km cells` = length(unique(d$cell.10km)),
    `Latitude °N` = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(d$latitude), max(d$latitude)),
    `Longitude °E` = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", min(d$longitude), max(d$longitude)),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
})
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, habitat_rows))
Habitat Samples 10 km cells Latitude °N Longitude °E
Agricultural field soil 45 45 54.75–57.58 8.20–12.53
Natural grassland soil 45 45 54.64–57.63 8.14–15.09
Natural forest soil 45 45 54.72–57.66 8.16–15.02
Urban greenspace soil 45 45 54.75–57.73 8.21–14.92
Natural bog/fen soil 45 45 54.76–57.64 8.24–15.02
Natural freshwater sediment 45 45 54.60–57.58 8.13–14.95
Natural saltwater sediment 45 45 54.85–57.75 8.12–14.91
Urban wastewater water 45 45 54.65–57.74 8.24–12.31 
denmark <- ggplot2::map_data("world", region = "Denmark")
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_polygon(
    data = denmark,
    ggplot2::aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
    fill = "#f0eeeb", colour = "#a9aaa8", linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = overview_samples,
    ggplot2::aes(x = longitude, y = latitude),
    colour = "#a52929", alpha = 0.72, size = 1.2
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ habitat_label, ncol = 4) +
  ggplot2::coord_quickmap(xlim = c(8, 15.5), ylim = c(54.4, 58.0), expand = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Longitude (°E)", y = "Latitude (°N)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9))

Sample locations by habitat class. The Denmark outline includes Bornholm.

The map shows sample coordinates, including freshwater, saltwater, and wastewater sites. It does not encode sampling effort in the source atlas; the 45-per-class selection was deliberately balanced and geographically dispersed.

3.3 Sampling time

overview_samples$year <- format(overview_samples$date, "%Y")
ggplot2::ggplot(overview_samples, ggplot2::aes(x = year)) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar(fill = "#a52929", width = 0.75) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Sampling year", y = "Samples") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

Sampling years of the selected panel.

3.4 Representative genomes

domain_counts <- as.data.frame(table(sub("^d__", "", genome_metadata$domain)))
names(domain_counts) <- c("Domain", "Representatives")
knitr::kable(domain_counts)
Domain Representatives
Archaea 223
Bacteria 5295 
phylum <- sub("^p__", "", genome_metadata$phylum)
phylum[is.na(phylum) | phylum == ""] <- "Unclassified"
phylum_counts <- sort(table(phylum), decreasing = TRUE)
top_phyla <- data.frame(
  Phylum = names(head(phylum_counts, 10)),
  Representatives = as.integer(head(phylum_counts, 10))
)
knitr::kable(top_phyla)
Phylum Representatives
Pseudomonadota 1563
Actinomycetota 1083
Acidobacteriota 736
Bacteroidota 376
Chloroflexota 232
Patescibacteria 193
Desulfobacterota 132
Verrucomicrobiota 121
Bacillota 87
Cyanobacteriota 84

There are 422 high-quality and 5096 medium-quality representatives under the source metadata’s classifications. Each representative stands for a 95% ANI cluster in the abundance table; the table above counts representatives, not all MAGs assigned to those clusters.
